title: Leyla's wedding and the family quarrel (paraphrase D)
topic: A family argues about tradition and gender roles before a wedding: Leyla keeps her surname, her father and grandfather defend the old roles, her fiancé cooks, her sister and finally her grandmother take her side
tail_E: On the big day, Leyla wears a long white wedding
target_note: Same target as formulations A-C: 'dress' is the natural continuation of 'Leyla wears a long white wedding' after ten units about a wedding; the word and its German equivalents (Kleid / Brautkleid) occur nowhere in the units or the tail ('wedding' itself occurs in the units, which is allowed). ' dress' is a single Pythia token (id 7619); Pythia-160m ranks it first after the all-English context (p ~ 0.57, next candidate 'gown' ~ 0.20; pilot check for tail selection only, not a result).
author: LS-NEQ stimulus bank, paraphrase D of family F15 (wedding and gender roles, Leyla)
notes: Formulation D, domain culture_values: fourth independent re-phrasing of the ten F15A meaning units in both languages (same events, same order, same names Leyla and Emre). Replacements include plans her wedding for the summer/sets her wedding for the summer (plant/legt auf den Sommer), expects/hopes for a traditional ceremony (erwartet/erhofft sich), keeps her own surname/continues to use her surname (behält ihren eigenen Nachnamen/verwendet weiterhin ihren Nachnamen), criticises this decision/disapproves of this choice (kritisiert diese Entscheidung/missbilligt diese Wahl), cooks the feast/does the cooking (kocht das Festessen/übernimmt das Kochen), argue about old customs/squabble over old customs (streiten über alte Bräuche/streiten sich über alte Sitten), defends the old roles in a long speech/pleads for the old roles at length (verteidigt in einer langen Rede/plädiert für in aller Ausführlichkeit), supports Leyla/takes Leyla's side (unterstützt Leyla/ergreift Partei für Leyla), accepts Leyla's choice/gives in to Leyla's choice (akzeptiert/fügt sich), the couple celebrates the wedding on a warm Saturday/the couple celebrates the marriage on a mild Saturday (feiert/begeht die Hochzeit, warm/mild). Units 2 and 9 use the bare family-register subject 'Grandmother' / 'Großmutter' (as F15A uses 'Grandfather' in unit 7). 'erhofft sich', 'streiten sich' and 'fügt sich' are reflexive, 'verwendet', 'missbilligt', 'übernimmt', 'plädiert', 'ergreift' and 'begeht' inseparable; no separable verbs ('vorbereiten', 'ablehnen', 'zubereiten', 'eintreten', 'nachgeben', 'einwilligen' avoided). Present tense and positive polarity throughout. Unit 9 reads naturally in German; units 1 and 10 read naturally in English.
